apollo-11.caption: The Apollo 11 landing site from 50 km up: the descent stage left on the surface, and West crater to the east.
apollo-11.credit: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University, LRO Narrow Angle Camera (SVS 10595)

apollo-14.caption: The Apollo 14 site at Fra Mauro: the Antares descent stage, the ALSEP experiments and Cone crater, with the astronauts' foot trails.
apollo-14.credit: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University, LRO Narrow Angle Camera (SVS 10595)

lunokhod-1.caption: Lunokhod 1 (arrow), the Soviet rover found again by LRO in 2010, 40 years after it landed.
lunokhod-1.credit: NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University, LRO Narrow Angle Camera (SVS 10595)

copernicus.caption: Inside Copernicus crater, photographed by Lunar Orbiter 2 in November 1966: the "picture of the century".
copernicus.credit: NASA / Lunar Orbiter Image Recovery Project, Lunar Orbiter 2 frame 2162 H3 (SVS 30128)

apollo-15.caption: Hadley Rille and the Apennine front around the Apollo 15 landing site, with Hadley Delta on the left.
apollo-15.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, rendered from LRO LOLA heights and LROC images (SVS 4918)

apollo-16.caption: The Apollo 16 site in the Descartes highlands, with the astronauts' traverses and North Ray crater.
apollo-16.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, rendered from LRO data (SVS 4989)

apollo-17.caption: The Taurus-Littrow valley of Apollo 17, with the routes driven on the lunar rover.
apollo-17.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, Tour of the Moon, from LRO data (SVS 4619)

tycho.caption: Tycho crater, 85 km across, with its central peak, seen obliquely.
tycho.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, Tour of the Moon, from LRO data (SVS 4619)

shackleton-rim.caption: How often each part of the south pole is sunlit (white: almost always, black: never). Shackleton crater is the round black floor at the centre.
shackleton-rim.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, LOLA average illumination (SVS 4770)

shackleton-rim.caption: Earth low on the horizon above the Shackleton rim, as it always stays from the south pole.
shackleton-rim.credit: NASA Goddard SVS, rendered from LOLA heights (SVS 4944)
